weekly.title: Egypt Arrests 6 Matsaddash Journalists on Claims of Spreading Disinformation
weekly.summary: The government claims that reporters from Matsaddash, a well-known news outlet that debunks false reports, spread disinformation for the banned Muslim Brotherhood.

weekly.title: Help! Air Canada Got Me to Europe, Then Stranded Me There.
weekly.summary: The airline helpfully rebooked a delayed traveler from Toronto, but failed to mention it had also canceled her return trip. She spent $800 to get home.

weekly.title: France rocked by student riots as hundreds arrested, violence spreads nationwide
weekly.summary: Violent student protests continue to spread across France, with school blockades, clashes with police and officials warning of outside agitators.

weekly.title: EXCLUSIVE: Trump’s new security alliance faces first real-world test deep in South America as troops deploy
weekly.summary: Donald Trump's Shield of the Americas faces its first real test as Bolivia deploys forces to strategic routes amid renewed blockade and unrest fears.

weekly.title: Hezbollah received $157M in weapons in 2024, mostly from 1 nation, report says
weekly.summary: The Israeli Center for Research of Terror Financing found Iran gave Hezbollah $129 million in rockets, missiles, drones and anti-tank missiles in 2024.

weekly.title: FlyDubai pilot showed world 'the highest form of courage,' India's PM says
weekly.summary: India Prime Minister Narendra Modi said India is saluting Smit Machchhar for his heroics onboard a FlyDubai plane that made an emergency landing.

weekly.title: Trump Dangles Alaska Gas Project as Part of Korean Investment Package
weekly.summary: The long-delayed project, which the developer has not yet formally greenlit, would deliver Alaskan gas to Asian markets but take several years to construct.

weekly.title: New York Times Reporting Through a Front Page That Never Published and More
weekly.summary: Times reporters and editors discuss items that have shaped our coverage, including Dean Baquet on the “Madam President” front page that never was.

weekly.title: Inside Binance Founder Changpeng Zhao’s Life After Prison
weekly.summary: Changpeng Zhao, jailed in the United States for a financial crime and pardoned by President Trump, is now living a gilded life in the United Arab Emirates.

weekly.title: The Global Bond Rout Reaches Worrying New Levels
weekly.summary: Investors are on alert as the yield on the 10-year Treasury note hit a new multi-decade high. The sell-off is also broadening in Europe, too.

weekly.title: What’s Next for ‘Hard Fork’?
weekly.summary: The podcast’s next chapter begins this week.

weekly.title: How Middle East Oil Exports Started Recovering
weekly.summary: Our business reporter Peter Eavis describes how oil exports from the Middle East have rebounded this month, getting closer to the levels seen before the Iran war.

weekly.title: Billion-dollar power link connecting Israel to Europe hits roadblock in bitter regional feud
weekly.summary: Cyprus accuses Recep Tayyip Erdoğan of blocking the Great Sea Interconnector energy project linking Israel, Cyprus and Greece amid maritime disputes.

weekly.title: Oil Is Flowing From the Persian Gulf, but Prices Remain High. Why?
weekly.summary: Crude oil costs close to $100 a barrel because traders are worried hostilities could soon restart and the world is burning through its emergency stockpiles.

weekly.title: When Data Centers Cluster Together, How Dirty Are They? One County Wants Answers.
weekly.summary: An unusual study aims to estimate the pollution and health costs from a cluster of proposed data centers, instead of considering each one separately.

weekly.title: Bessent Settled Tax Issue That Had Put Him at Odds With I.R.S.
weekly.summary: The Treasury Secretary had previously taken a position on his taxes that contradicted the views of the tax agency that he now oversees.

weekly.title: Mattel Chief Named Co-C.E.O. of Combined Paramount and Warner Bros.
weekly.summary: Ynon Kreiz, who will work alongside David Ellison at the merged company, helped turn Barbie into a blockbuster movie.

weekly.title: OpenAI’s Greg Brockman Backs Out of Second $25 Million Donation to A.I. Super PAC
weekly.summary: Greg Brockman, OpenAI’s president and co-founder, said internally that the super PAC, Leading the Future, had become a “distraction” for the A.I. company.

weekly.title: While Surging to Records, Stocks Experience Some ‘Wobbles’
weekly.summary: Beneath the S&P 500’s 2 percent gain in the third quarter, the rise in oil prices and bond yields led some investors to become more cautious about the outlook for A.I. profits.

weekly.title: Google Wants Hollywood to Stop Being So Afraid of Technology
weekly.summary: 100 Zeros, a collaboration between Google and Range Media Partners, aims to give the tech giant a foothold in movies, TV and emerging forms of entertainment.

weekly.title: Google Releases New Gemini Model With Guardrails Amid A.I. Safety Debate
weekly.summary: For safety reasons, Gemini 4 Argon will initially be available only to some companies and organizations focused on cybersecurity defense before it is more widely released, Google said.

weekly.title: How to Listen to Your Favorite Music, Online or Off the Grid
weekly.summary: Streaming services can introduce you to a wonderland of nearly unlimited audio, but downloading your digital collection has advantages.

weekly.title: Trump Media’s Merger With Nuclear Fusion Company Moves Closer to Completion
weekly.summary: A securities filing laid out the terms of the deal between Truth Social’s parent company and TAE Technologies, which was formally announced in December.

weekly.title: Fed’s Watchdog Finds No Misconduct or Illegal Activity in Costly Renovations
weekly.summary: A new report by the Federal Reserve’s independent inspector general concluded that a nearly $2.5 billion construction project was poorly managed but made no referrals to the U.S. attorney general.

weekly.title: F.T.C. Investigates OpenAI and Anthropic Over Potential Consumer Harms
weekly.summary: The agency will examine whether A.I. labs have broken federal laws prohibiting companies from unfair and deceptive practices.

weekly.summary: Epic’s engineers deployed an Anthropic tool that exposed security risks that could allow undetected access to millions of patient records.

weekly.title: He Was a Tech Investor Before There Was a Silicon Valley
weekly.summary: Bill Draper began funding start-ups in the early 1960s, when the Santa Clara Valley was better known for apricot orchards than microchips. He has died at 98.

weekly.title: E.E.O.C. Sues Harvard for Data on Diversity in Hiring Practices
weekly.summary: The Equal Employment Opportunity Commission filed a lawsuit asking a judge to compel the university to provide information on hiring practices that the agency said discriminated against white men.

weekly.title: Moscow threatens nuclear response over tiny fortress wedged between US allies as clash fears grow
weekly.summary: Russia's nuclear threat over Kaliningrad raises alarm as experts warn the Baltic exclave is already a hub for hybrid warfare against NATO allies.

weekly.title: Irish PM says Ireland ‘not overrun’ by immigrants, legal migration tied to economic success
weekly.summary: Micheál Martin addresses Ireland's demographic change as nearly one in four in Ireland are born abroad as the government moves to tighten asylum, citizenship and immigration rules.

weekly.title: Evangelical leader slams Palestinian official’s Bible claims as ‘contemptible’
weekly.summary: Influential Pastor John Hagee slams Palestinian Ambassador Husam Zomlot's claim that the Bible is a "Palestinian book," calling it an attempt to erase Jewish history.

weekly.title: Taiwan analysts say Trump-Xi summit produced no policy shift but real test lies ahead
weekly.summary: Taiwan analysts assess whether Xi Jinping secured private concessions from Trump, with arms sales and senior U.S. official visits as key tests ahead.

weekly.summary: The U.S. military completed its withdrawal from Erbil Air Base, ending Operation Inherent Resolve in Iraq while relocating its headquarters to Jordan.

weekly.title: FlyDubai passenger says co-pilot stabbed captain before terrifying plunge, emergency landing
weekly.summary: A passenger says a FlyDubai co-pilot stabbed the captain before the Israel-bound flight plunged, triggering hijacking fears and an emergency diversion.

weekly.title: How Meta Uses A.I. Data Centers to Avoid Billions in Federal Taxes
weekly.summary: Meta is exploiting a lucrative tax break intended to support research and experimentation. Its own accountants say the gambit is risky.

weekly.summary: In a series of private meetings, the company consulted religious scholars to help instill morality into its A.I. models — and make the case that Claude could be conscious.

weekly.title: At A.I. Event, Trump Asks Meta, OpenAI and Microsoft to Make Safety Decisions Themselves
weekly.summary: President Trump’s meetings with tech leaders produced some voluntary safeguards and a commitment to rebrand artificial intelligence as “super intelligence,” the term that Mr. Trump prefers.

weekly.title: OpenAI Ignored Employees’ Warnings About Safely Testing A.I. Models
weekly.summary: Employees and security researchers said that they had cautioned the company on safely testing its A.I. models and strengthening its corporate infrastructure, but that OpenAI did not listen.

weekly.title: Ukrainian Science Academy, Struck by Drone, Played Key Role in Research
weekly.summary: Over 90 percent of Ukraine’s scientific discoveries have been attributed to Ukraine’s National Academy of Sciences, including advancements in astronomy and military technology.

weekly.title: OpenAI Unveils Dots, New A.I. Agents to Rival Meta’s Muse
weekly.summary: The ChatGPT maker unveiled agents that act as assistants, just weeks after Meta released Muse, as it faces scrutiny over incidents involving its technology.

weekly.summary: The Yom Kippur attack outside Sons of Jacob Synagogue in Belleville has intensified demands for armed security at Jewish institutions across Canada.

weekly.summary: The company’s researchers raised questions about the security of the model, known as GPT-6.1 Astra.

weekly.summary: The increase comes four months after the chip giant added $80 billion to its buyback program, bringing the total remaining authorized amount to $235 billion.
